RUN-001.notes: Authoritative runtime: Run/Turn/Step/Attempt transitions evaluated inside the event-emitting transaction (illegal transitions roll back state and events together), generation fencing before any write, attempts appended never overwritten, cancellation and suspension as authoritative transitions, and recovery that applies next_safe_action (a WAITING_* run is released only by its matching resolution, an unsettled effect is reconciled never retried) and is idempotent across repeated calls. Turn-loop seams (model proposal, tool dispatch, delegation, verification) return typed not-available errors naming INT-002/RUN-011/RUN-002/RUN-008 rather than fabricating success. Two deviations are recorded: the runtime commits through EventStore::commit_mutation_tx instead of crates/graph because graph depends on the server's schema module (consolidation steps in HANDOFF.md), and the parity of both state tables with the database constraints is enforced by tests/architecture/test_runtime_state_parity.py added during integration. Also fixed a real CORE-006 defect found by the recovery test: cancellation_at is TIMESTAMPTZ and was decoded as a String.

RUN-002.notes: AgentThread lifecycle for teammates and workers on one primitive with a policy rule (teammates never JOIN, workers terminate only from JOINED), an exactly-once durable mailbox cursor, delegation that calls the narrowing check before any insert (a widening check writes nothing), handoff with a PENDING durable record that a restarted runtime can complete or roll back and that is idempotent when re-completed, and fanout join that parks the parent until the last child joins and never double-merges. During integration three follow-ups were added: the state-parity guard now covers AgentThreadStatus against the database constraint, DOMAIN §9.2 gained the two mailbox event names additively (agent.mailbox_delivered, agent.mailbox_cursor_advanced) so authority matches the contract, and the dev-stack integration test now runs in its own compose project on offset ports so its reset/volume teardown can no longer destroy a stack shared by other agents.

RUN-003.notes: Model proposals are compiled and validated before touching the graph: bounded by the policy max_plan_nodes (25 when no policy row), malformed input rejected with VALIDATION_SCHEMA while writing nothing, acyclicity checked over existing depends_on/parent_of edges, parent_id chains and the proposal's own additions, CompletionContract ownership or explicit inheritance recorded per node, capability needs checked with RUN-005's narrowing algebra, and base_revision compare-and-set enforced before the single GraphTransaction applies the batch. Determinism is proven by applying the same proposal against the same starting state twice (identical revision, aggregate/event type sequence and node shape) and once after a simulated restart; replay after acceptance fails with the revision conflict; work.plan_proposed/applied/rejected are emitted exactly once. Known limitation recorded in HANDOFF: CORE-005's CreateWorkNode generates node ids inside the transaction without an alias, so a plan cannot yet reference a node it creates in the same batch (intra-plan parents/edges are validated then rejected with VALIDATION_SCHEMA). Fix planned before RUN-011 wires the planner into the turn loop.

RUN-004.notes: Bounded-concurrency orchestration over the canonical WorkGraph. crates/server/src/runtime/orchestration owns the execution decisions: a deterministic ready queue (priority then id), dependency release (draft/blocked -> ready once every depends_on prerequisite is done; -> blocked when one failed or was cancelled), fan-in joins (a waiting parent joins once its last child is done and is blocked if a child can never finish), a capacity gate counted from durable run state, cancellation propagation down work_nodes.parent_id with dependents blocked, and durable waits obeyed by never selecting a node whose run is parked or suspended. depends_on reads `from` depends on `to` (documented on WorkEdgeKind), so `to` is the prerequisite; orchestration refuses a cyclic snapshot instead of selecting from a graph it cannot reason about. Every started run goes through the existing scheduler RunDispatch port into the canonical Run state machine, so there is no second scheduler or orchestration authority; every node transition goes through a WorkGraphPort whose production implementation applies it as one event-emitting GraphTransaction, proven in crates/graph/tests/orchestration.rs against the real store (one revision bump per batch, a stale replay conflicts, and a dependent is never releasable while any prerequisite is unfinished). Concurrency is counted from durable run state (RUNNING/VERIFYING hold a slot; QUEUED and parked runs do not), so the bound survives a restart and two instances agree; the limit itself is supplied by the caller because RUN-010 owns budget enforcement, and a saturated limit is a typed BUDGET_EXHAUSTED refusal rather than a silent drop. Cancellation converges under a storm: runs go through the one authoritative RuntimeStore::cancel (idempotent, one run.cancelled per run, a lost transaction race counted as already-cancelled), the node batch is revision compare-and-set with bounded recomputation, and work a caller actually cancelled is reported even when a later retry wins the graph race. Two limits are recorded rather than papered over: the Run state machine has no QUEUED -> CANCELLED edge, so an unstarted run inside a cancelled subtree is reported (runs_left_unstarted) and never dispatched instead of being cancelled; and the graph-backed port's wiring belongs to the composition root (APP-001), exactly as PlanWorkspacePort does.

RUN-005.notes: Capability algebra composes grants by intersection with most-restrictive constraints (max_tier=min, approval only toward ask/never, earliest expiry, smallest budget) over all nine DOMAIN §6.1 selector kinds; projection assembly follows the fixed §6.2 layer order, ignores and records any widening as capability.widening_rejected naming the layer, and fails closed with an empty projection plus CAPABILITY_INPUTS_UNAVAILABLE when an input layer is unavailable or a policy has a gap at tier >= 1; authorize() always re-checks the current inputs digest and expiry so a stale projection cannot authorize dispatch; delegation narrowing is implemented for RUN-002's hook. During integration the architecture gate's new-persistent-store rule was corrected: capability owns capability_projections, so it is an allowed store owner, and the rule's fixtures now cover every table-owning module.

RUN-006.notes: Evaluation order is RBAC -> capability projection -> trust escalation -> privacy -> sequence guards -> policy rules -> receipt requirement -> user rules, with tenant and workspace policies merged most-restrictively (deny>ask>allow) and no matching rule at effective tier >= 1 denying. Tier 4 always asks: an always user rule is rejected on store and ignored on evaluation. Receipts bind id/request/effect/approver/params_digest/scope/generation/expiry and are signed with HMAC-SHA256 under a server key from QUANSIO_APPROVAL_SIGNING_KEY (absent key fails closed); verification is constant-time and single-use, so a receipt for one action cannot authorize a changed one, and nothing is written on failure. A parameter change supersedes a pending request with one approval.superseded event. Escalation follows DOMAIN §12 rule 2 (tier >= 2 derived from UNTRUSTED_EXTERNAL escalates one tier) rather than the brief's paraphrase, and escalated proposals cannot use always. Trust labelling arrives through an injected source, fail-closed until INT-012.

RUN-007.notes: Universal Effect Ledger: reservation derives the idempotency key from effect class, resource and params digest and leans on the schema's partial unique in-flight index, so racing dispatchers reserve exactly one action and an in-flight duplicate is a typed conflict; every transition is one event-emitting transaction with exactly one effect.* event and contiguous aggregate versions; settlement is terminal and re-settlement refuses before writing; an OUTCOME_UNKNOWN record cannot be retried (typed refusal) and is resolved only by reconciliation matching the class strategy from config/effects.yaml (validated against the generated catalog and failing closed on any divergence); a retry creates a new identity sharing the key and never touches the old row; approval-required actions cannot bypass the receipt; protocol state keeps next_safe_action on ReconcileEffect until settled; all reads are tenant-scoped.

RUN-011.notes: The turn loop now owns a real ToolCall path. crates/tools holds the Tool contract and a control-plane Tool Registry loaded from config/tools.yaml: namespaced versioned declarations, a strict JSON-Schema subset whose unknown keywords fail the load (so a schema can never be silently under-enforced), every object schema closing additionalProperties, argument validation that rejects unknown or missing fields, derivation of effect class (static or arg-driven, e.g. fs.write scope), resource selector, canonical parameter digest and idempotency key, per-tool host, output bound, timeout, cancellability, evidence capture and source trust, plus exposure filtered by the capability projection. The generated catalog (schemas/catalog/tools.yaml) and the registry must cover each other exactly; connector/scm families are reserved catalog entries that are not callable until CAP-003 and EXEC-009/012 register concrete operations. crates/server/src/runtime/turn_loop implements DOMAIN §7.4 in the fixed order registry -> schema -> capability projection -> policy/RBAC/user rules -> approval park -> Effect Ledger reservation with a dispatch token -> host execution -> settlement, with the durable tool_calls row (migration 0007 records the declaration version) and tool.* RuntimeEvents. Independent calls are dispatched concurrently and their results applied in proposal order; the engine now parks a run for approval, resumes the recorded call instead of re-proposing it, and reports an unsettled effect for reconciliation rather than re-dispatching. The question protocol (user.ask and the model's question) writes a durable Question with the policy TTL, parks WAITING_QUESTION and resumes on the answer or expires the run; delegation, plan and memory routes go to their owning ports and fail closed with the owner named. Fail-closed choices: a refusal before the reservation writes no EffectRecord and reaches no host; the proposal's causal chain is evaluated from UNTRUSTED_EXTERNAL until INT-005 supplies real context labels, so a tier >= 2 call is escalated and needs a receipt. Host incident during this run (now resolved): for part of the session the machine would not execute newly created binaries, so `cargo test` could not spawn freshly linked binaries; the suites were run by writing the linked binary into a pre-existing inode and the counts were later reproduced exactly by a clean `cargo test`. Once the host recovered, `bash scripts/ci/ci.sh` ran green on main (all eleven baseline gates) at the RUN-011 merge 69a7d20f4c7f. See HANDOFF.md 'Environment requirements' for the incident, the workaround and the artifact repair. No test was skipped, weakened or excused.
